subject: health
topic: After a long day awake you perform like someone who has been drinking
angle: While prolonged wakefulness often produces impairments equivalent to moderate alcohol levels, the specific magnitude of that impairment varies significantly depending on the cognitive task and the statistical method used.
title: The Cost of Staying Awake

hooks.text: Are you sober when you are tired?
You think you are alert. The data suggests otherwise.
You are operating on a borrowed consciousness.

reveal.headline: Your tired brain mirrors a drunk one.
reveal.body: After 20-25 hours of wakefulness, your performance decrements can equal a blood alcohol concentration of 0.10%.

explain.headline: The impairment depends on what you do.
explain.body: Evidence is mixed. Fatigue may match 0.05% BAC in some tests but 0.10% in others. The severity depends on the specific task and the method used to measure it.

matters.headline: Your alertness is not a constant.
matters.body: That may be why your ability to drive or learn fluctuates. Your brain does not fail all at once, but degrades specific functions at different rates.

example.headline: The late night drive.
example.body: You sit in your car at 2 a.m. The road is clear. Your hands feel heavy on the wheel as you try to stay focused on the white lines.

question.headline: How much of your day is lived in a haze?

claims.text: After 24 h of sustained wakefulness and with 0.08%BAC, individuals showed maximal cognitive impairment; however, the magnitude of impairment found for fatigue was equivalent only to that observed for 0.05%BAC.
claims.quote: After 24 h of sustained wakefulness and with 0.08%BAC, individuals showed maximal cognitive impairment; however, the magnitude of impairment found for fatigue was equivalent only to that observed for 0.05%BAC.

claims.text: Fatigue caused greater impairment than alcohol on the speed of continuous attention and memory and learning, and on the accuracy of complex matching.
claims.quote: It was demonstrated that fatigue caused greater impairment than alcohol on the speed of continuous attention and memory and learning, and on the accuracy of complex matching.

claims.text: Acute sleep deprivation produced a disproportionate risk to driving safety by selectively and rapidly degrading operational vehicle control compared to cumulative sleep restriction.
claims.quote: cumulative sleep restriction produced only limited changes in driving performance, whereas acute sleep deprivation produced a disproportionate risk to driving safety by selectively and rapidly degrading operational vehicle control.

claims.text: After 17-19 hours without sleep, performance on some tests was equivalent or worse than that at a BAC of 0.05%.
claims.quote: After 17-19 hours without sleep, corresponding to 2230 and 0100, performance on some tests was equivalent or worse than that at a BAC of 0.05%.

claims.text: After longer periods without sleep, performance reached levels equivalent to the maximum alcohol dose given to subjects (BAC of 0.1%).
claims.quote: After longer periods without sleep, performance reached levels equivalent to the maximum alcohol dose given to subjects (BAC of 0. 1%).

claims.text: Approximately 20-25 h of wakefulness produced performance decrements equivalent to those observed at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0.10%.
claims.quote: equating the performance impairment in the two conditions indicated that, depending on the task measured, approximately 20-25 h of wakefulness produced performance decrements equivalent to those observed at a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of 0. 10%.

verdict: The evidence shows that sleep deprivation causes significant cognitive and motor impairments that can match alcohol intoxication, but the severity of these effects is task-dependent and may be overestimated in some studies.
caveat: The magnitude of fatigue-related impairment is highly dependent on the specific task measured and the statistical methods used to account for performance variability.
caption:
Sleep deprivation creates cognitive impairments that can mirror alcohol intoxication.

Research shows these effects vary by task and statistical method. Some studies find fatigue matches lower alcohol levels, while others show it reaches much higher levels.

How many hours of wakefulness are you pushing your body to endure?
